summary.text: St. Isaac, son of St. Abraham, belongs to the biblical covenant story and is commemorated among the righteous Patriarchs before Christ’s Nativity.
summary.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

saints.context: The source’s received ecclesiastical narrative is identified as such. Uncertain dates, later traditions and unknown circumstances of death are retained as uncertain.

blocks.text: St. Isaac is the child promised to St. Abraham and his wife in old age. Genesis connects his birth with God’s covenant and later recounts the testing of Abraham, in which Isaac is bound for sacrifice but spared when God provides a ram.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: Genesis describes his marriage, the birth of his two sons, and a period of famine. God renews the promise given to Abraham and commands Isaac to remain in the land. Disputes over wells and an agreement with a neighboring ruler form part of his life in Gerar and Beersheba. The account of the blessing of St. Jacob also records conflict and deception within the family.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: Genesis gives St. Isaac’s age at death as 180 and says that his sons bury him. The text presents a death in old age, not an execution or martyrdom. No modern absolute date is supplied by this profile.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The OCA names St. Isaac as a righteous Patriarch among Christ’s ancestors. His commemoration belongs to the movable Sundays before the Nativity, so the date displayed in a sample-year article should not be treated as fixed.
